scope: POST /videos/:id/upload/parts, request/response DTOs and external-spec HTTP tests only.

implementation.handler: Global inherited JWT + CurrentUser.sub + ParseUUIDPipe; thin delegation to existing VideoUploadsService.signParts. Explicit HTTP200, JSON control only, real route throttle120/min.
implementation.input: DTO requires array of 1..50 unique integers >=1, no coercion. Existing service validates each number against persisted actual partCount, owner, draft, operation claim and expiry. No client key/upload_id/ETag authority; unknown properties rejected by inherited whitelist.
implementation.output: Typed parts with partNumber, signed consumer-origin url, absolute expiresAt and exact Content-Length string header; 64MiB full part and exact smaller remainder verified. Real signature deadline <=900s and never past session; near-expiry session caps TTL.
implementation.direct_upload: API issues permissions only. Real signed PUT of small final part arrives directly at MinIO, returns ETag and appears in authoritative ListParts; no complete-file allocation or binary traffic through API. Wrong actual length with matching changed Content-Length is rejected403 by storage signature; no part/outbox created.
implementation.security: Foreign/missing/no-channel404, missing/invalidJWT401, malformedUUID400, invalid batch400, active completing/aborting409, processing/aborted409, expired410, typed storage failure503. Safe inherited envelopes; tests verify no partial permission returned on failures. Existing creation/auth limits unchanged.
implementation.openapi: Regenerated through existing compiled export pipeline. JSON assertions prove UUID/JWT, required JSON input, unique integer items, min1/max50, HTTP200, nested Content-Length header, URI/date-time and common errors400/401/404/409/410/413/429/503. All previously committed operations unchanged. Only integer array items and constant maxItems require explicit request metadata because CLI plugin could not infer them; other array constraints come from validators.
